hook.text: DNA can't leave the nucleus. It sends a messenger instead—a copy made of RNA. The message must get out.

buildup.text: RNA polymerase reads one DNA strand and builds a matching messenger RNA. It's like photocopying one page.

discovery.text: The mRNA copy travels through nuclear pores into the cytoplasm where protein-building machinery waits.

twist.text: Before leaving, the mRNA is edited. Introns are cut out, exons are spliced together. The rough draft gets polished.

climax.text: One gene can produce multiple proteins by splicing exons differently. Same recipe, different dishes.

punchline.text: DNA stays home. RNA carries the instructions out.

quiz.question: What carries genetic instructions from nucleus to cytoplasm?
